what: Heico makes replacement parts for jet engines and aircraft that are approved by regulators as alternatives to the original manufacturer's parts, usually at a lower price. It also makes electronic equipment for defence, space and medical uses.
customers: Airlines, maintenance providers, defence contractors and space companies.
money: approved replacement parts, repair and overhaul services
electronics for defence, space, medical and industrial uses
moat: Thousands of individual regulatory approvals built up over decades, each one a licence to sell a part the original manufacturer would rather sell itself.
risks: Its parts compete directly with engine makers who control the aftermarket
Airline maintenance spending falls in a downturn
Growth depends partly on continuous small acquisitions
The shares trade at a high multiple of earnings
opportunities: Revenue grew about 16% last year and about 27% a year over three years
Airlines flying older aircraft for longer raises demand for replacement parts
Operating margin of 23% with a long record of family-led capital discipline
watch: Flight Support organic growth and new part approvals.
